newsitem.title: USA: Summit Bancorp reports strong profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Summit Bancorp reports strong profit rise.

text.p: Summit Bancorp said Wednesday its profits rose strongly in the lastest quarter, due in part to a string of acquisitions in the past year.

The Princeton, N.J.-based company said its net income rose to $74 million, or 79 cents a share, from $62.2 million, or 70 cents a share. Excluding a one-time special assessment to the Savings Association Insurance Fund, operating earnings in the latest quarter were $80.7 million, or 86 cents per share.
"These strong operating results have enabled us to achieve the profitability and efficiency goals we anticipated reaching in 1997," Chairman T. Joseph Semrod said.

"In the past year, Summit has completed or announced acquisitions in our market area representing more than $7 billion in assets and nearly $6 billion in deposits," Semrod said. "These acquisitions strengthen our market presence, and their successful integration provides improved efficiencies and profitability."
Summit Bancorporation was acquired in March 1 by UJB Financial Corp., and the combined company was renamed Summit Bancorp.

Prior to that, Summit Bancorporation had acquired Garden State Bancshares in January, and UJB had acquired Flemington National Bank and Trust Co. in February of this year and Bancorp New Jersey in July, 1995. In August of this year, Summit agreed to acquire B.M.J. Financial Corp., which operates The Bank of Mid-Jersey.

Summit Bancorp operates more than 360 community banking offices and supermarket branches of Summit Bank in New Jersey and eastern Pennsylvania. Summit's stock was 12.5 cents higher at $39.625 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
